name: Letterboxx
soft_passes: #1 self-masked transparent squircle (baked corners), not HIG square full-bleed layers
#4 16px squint: 'pale card in a blue container' gestalt survives but airmail striping smears to noise
#6 three chromatic families (teal + airmail-red + airmail-blue on cream); accent not reserved to one focal detail
failures: #3 silhouette collapses to a rounded-square tray blob — tray is the squircle, envelope detail never projects past the outline; identity is colour/material only
#10 fixed full-colour 3D render, baked teal background + baked lighting, no light/dark/clear/tinted layers — flattens to a blob in mono/tinted

palette.background: scene — glossy teal tray fills the squircle; body #479CAF, rim specular #97EAFF, deep occlusion #31718C->#0B2567

light_model: soft global illumination, key from upper-front; broad matte ambient occlusion under stack and inside tray; glossy specular along plastic tray rim; matte paper; no long shadows (system supplies drop shadow)
layer_stack: fanned pile of plain cream envelopes
teal tray front lip (occludes bottom of stack)
rhymes_hint: contemporary 3D-render / claymorphic soft-object icons (Blender/Spline/AI-3D lineage) and skeuomorphic-quote 'container full of literal objects' icons (tray/box/shelf holding artifacts); palette-family: teal container + red-white-blue airmail. Style-family guess: '3D object-tray, colour-dependent'.
notes: 256x256 web render (transparent-masked squircle, alpha=0 outside), not the 1024 master — stripes/flap seam already softened, so #4 judged slightly generously. Self-masked (baked corners) rather than HIG square full-bleed layers, which is why no system appearance variants exist (feeds #10). Strong icon<->app palette coherence: tray teal #479CAF matches the cover's teal->blue gradient; app UI is neutral gray/teal, so the airmail red/blue lives only in the icon. Reads as a mail/comms app, accurate to the newsletter-reader function despite the Productivity category. Non-negotiable generation checks 1-4: fails #3 outright and is borderline on #4 — a cautionary example that small-size legibility here rests on colour, not silhouette.
